To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) test cases can be generated from requirements, (2) test cases can also be generated from models, (3) requirements can be traced to test cases, (4) requirements can be mapped to models, and (5) models can be traced to requirements.

(1) test cases and requirements are formal equivalent, (2) the formalization of SysML allows for the automation of all steps of the test case generation process, (3) test case generation can be automated based on requirements, properties or models, and (4) the combination of all three approaches is needed to achieve guaranteed test strength

(1) the formal semantics of a modelling formalism is a key enabler for automated model based testing, (2) the formal semantics has to provide a formal definition of the notion of traceability, and (3) the formal semantics must provide the means for defining a test model that is equivalent to the requirements specification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an industrial strength test automation tool that is capable of supporting all three test paradigms and that is applicable to complex system development in safety critical domains.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
model based testing can be automated to a very high degree.
model based testing is the only viable option for testing safety critical systems.

the application of formal methods is key enabler for achieving the degree automation that is needed to effectively test today's safety critical software intensive systems with acceptable effort, while achieving the degree of comprehensively that is required by the applicable certification standards.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of formal semantics in the context of SysML allows us to achieve the degree of automation required for industrial strength testing of complex systems.
model based testing is a key technology for testing complex systems, but that the technology needs to evolve in the direction of industrial strength automation.

we have developed a model based test automation tool that is capable of handling large and complex models, that it can be applied to a broad variety of modelling formalisms and test strategies, and that it is integrated with the industrial verification and validation work flows.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a formal semantics for the model formalism is essential for achieving a fully automated testing process, as soon as a model has been elaborated and requirements have been associated with the model elements.
model based testing is a viable approach to automated testing of safety critical systems.

the combination of formal methods and model based testing is an effective way to achieve the required degree of comprehensibility and test strength for the verification and validation of safety critical systems.
